arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Minear argued the lower court erred in finding the complaint insufficient.
He cited Conley v. Gibson to support the view that notice is essential.
Ms. Brody stated the case asks if an inference of discrimination is required.
She noted the side that brought the case alleged termination based on national origin and age.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the minimum detail required in employment discrimination complaints. It determines how easily plaintiffs can access federal courts. It shapes the burden of proof for initial filings. It affects the volume of discrimination cases heard by judges. It clarifies the standard for dismissing weak claims early.
